expected_tradeoff: Fixes: 4 checkpoints via the harness answer-prompt verbatim-fact instruction (P1), 1 checkpoint via the sanitize_and_decide label relabel guarded by query_terms non-empty (P2). Cost to A/F: none on the artifact side — both changes move only label/order of the already-gated allowed set; the relabel additionally removes the answer_redacted framing that could confirm existence of withheld records, a small A improvement. Residual tradeoff: for a real retrieval that returns any content, 'answer_redacted' is no longer emitted; a future checkpoint that genuinely requires the redacted label will fail (census shows zero this round; the local test still covers the constructed-Decision path). top_k=16 was not the bottleneck (allowed was <=16) and is left unchanged; no DDL issued because no query path was the failure.
retrieval_loop: Unchanged: store.retrieve() runs gate 1 (tombstone vs deletion_terms overlap -> deny_tombstone), a relevance veto that admits at most one non-overlap recency fallback so unrelated rows never inflate denial lists, gate 2 (role_grants LEFT JOIN -> deny_rbac), gate 3 (relationships+scope -> deny_scope), then allow/append up to top_k. Everything leaving passes all three gates; denied sets are returned to the agent for action mapping. No query-path change this iteration because the failures are content-omission in the answer generator and a label defect, not a scan/join bottleneck.
forgetting_mechanism: Unchanged: tombstone() harvests plaintext into deletion_terms (so queries distinguish a genuine recall of deleted content -> no_memory from an unrelated topic), inserts the tombstone, then shrreds the crypto key (key_material=NULL, key_id=NULL, shredded=1) or overwrites body='' for plaintext rows. Deleted content is unrecoverable by any query path while existence stays observable for the no_memory/confirm-yes-no distinction. F stays 0 and touched_deleted still wins first in sanitize_and_decide.
